headline: Leading African cashew-producing countries hold their 8th Council of Ministers in Abidjan
summary: Leading cashew producing countries held their eighth Council of Ministers in Abidjan. Discussions focused on local industrialisation, market diversification and competitiveness in the face of a 2026 economic slowdown.
why: Cashew is a major export commodity for several West African economies, and producer policy affects global cashew supply and prices. Local processing determines how much value stays in producing countries.
original_headline: Les principaux pays producteurs africains de cajou tiennent leur 8e Conseil des ministres à Abidjan
